# Maintenance Request Workflow Optimization at Oakline Property Group

**Company and People**

*   **Company:** Oakline Property Group
    *   **What it does:** Manages approximately 340 units across six buildings.
*   **People:**
    *   Operations Manager (Speaker)
    *   Carlos (Maintenance Coordinator)
    *   Linda Park (Owner company representative)

**Workflow Steps**

| **Step** | **Who** | **Tool** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resident submits request via App Folio portal, email to leasing office, or text to Carlos | Resident | App Folio / Gmail / Text Message |
| Carlos checks portal, email, and texts; decides if emergency or routine | Carlos | App Folio / Gmail / Personal Cell Phone |
| For routine requests, assign to in-house technician or outside vendor from Excel list | Carlos | Excel Spreadsheet |
| Carlos calls or texts vendor to schedule appointment | Carlos | Personal Cell Phone |
| Carlos informs resident of scheduled vendor arrival time | Carlos | Personal Cell Phone |
| Carlos verifies vendor showed up (manual check) | Carlos | Memory / Notes |

**Volumes and Timing**

*   340 units managed across six buildings.
*   ~90 work orders per month.
*   ~15 emergencies per month (e.g., water leaks, no heat).
*   Repair approval required for any request over $500.
*   11 property owners involved in approvals.
*   Average days to close a work order: ~9 days.
*   Estimated status calls to leasing office: ~30 calls per week.
*   Vendor non-attendance rate: ~1 out of every 8 appointments.
*   Invoice matching issues occur ~2–3 times per month.

**Tools and Systems**

*   App Folio (Resident Portal and Work Orders)
*   Gmail
*   Personal Cell Phone (Carlos's)
*   Excel Spreadsheet (Vendor List)
*   Whiteboard (Open items tracking)
*   QuickBooks (Accounting/Vendor Invoices)

**Pain Points**

| **Pain** | **Cost or impact** |
| --- | --- |
| Vendors do not show up or arrive on wrong days; no record exists in the system. | Resident calls leasing office upset; status unknown because info is only in Carlos's texts. |
| Status calls consume significant office time. | ~30 calls per week to leasing office. |
| Approval delays for repairs over $500 due to varying owner response times. | Work orders remain open while residents wait; some take a week for approval. |
| Manual tracking of pending work orders via whiteboard. | Whiteboard is usually out of date. |
| Work orders stay open for weeks without closure. | Residents receive bad reviews thinking requests are ignored; monthly reports to owners show incorrect unfinished work counts. |
| After-hours emergency invoices cannot be matched to units because work orders were never created. | Bookkeeper must email Carlos; he must dig through texts to match invoice to unit. |
| Lack of continuity when Carlos is on vacation. | Operations manager covered, but lacked vendor numbers, job schedule visibility, and resident expectations were broken (e.g., promised vendors didn't show). |

**Desired Outcome and Measure**

*   **Outcome:** Every request (regardless of entry method) ends up in the App Folio within one hour, and every resident receives updates when a vendor is scheduled and when work is done without manual memory reliance by Carlos.
*   **Measure 1:** Reduce status calls to the leasing office from ~30 per week by 50%.
*   **Measure 2:** Reduce average days to close a work order from ~9 days.

**Decision Makers**

*   Operations Manager (Speaker)
*   Linda Park (Owner company representative)
*   Carlos (Maintenance Coordinator - required for input on operational details)

**Next Steps**

| **Owner** | **Action** | **When** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speaker (Operations Manager) | Export one month of work orders from Appfolio with names removed and send to Operations Manager | Monday |
| Speaker (Operations Manager) | Conduct short call with Linda Park and Carlos | Next week |
| Speaker (Operations Manager) | Present proposal for One Lane solution covering request intake and resident status updates as a pilot on the Magnolia Building | Following the next-week call |
